questions.question_text: Read the unseen passage about the migrating monarch butterflies. According to the text, what is the primary navigation method these butterflies use to reach their wintering grounds in Mexico?
options: A) They follow the wind currents along the coast
B) They use the magnetic pull of the earth and the sun's position
C) They follow older butterflies that have made the journey before
D) They rely entirely on scent trails left on trees
questions.answer: B) They use the magnetic pull of the earth and the sun's position

questions.question_text: Based on the passage, choose the word that is closest in meaning to 'perilous' as used to describe the butterflies' long journey.
questions.answer: C) Dangerous

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank based on the passage: The monarch butterflies depend heavily on the _________ plant to lay their eggs and feed their caterpillars.
questions.answer: A) Milkweed

questions.question_text: Why has the monarch butterfly population seen a significant decline over the past two decades according to the author? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The population has declined primarily due to the widespread loss of milkweed habitats caused by urban development and the heavy use of agricultural herbicides.

questions.question_text: What protective measures has the Mexican government implemented to safeguard the monarch's wintering forests? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The Mexican government has established protected biosphere reserves, strictly banned illegal logging in the area, and involved local communities in eco-tourism to preserve the forests.

questions.question_text: How can ordinary citizens contribute to the conservation of monarch butterflies in their own backyards? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Citizens can contribute by planting native milkweed and nectar-rich flowers in their gardens, and by avoiding the use of harmful chemical pesticides.

sections.section_name: Section B - Writing Skills & Applied Grammar

questions.question_text: Identify the option that correctly completes the sentence using the appropriate degree of the adjective: 'Of all the athletes in the tournament, Rahul was undoubtedly the ________.'
questions.answer: C) fastest

questions.question_text: Choose the correct sentence that uses the Present Perfect tense accurately.
options: A) She has finished her science project yesterday.
B) They have lived in this city since 2015.
C) We have go to the market an hour ago.
D) I had eaten my lunch already.
questions.answer: B) They have lived in this city since 2015.

questions.question_text: Select the correct relative pronoun to fill in the blank: 'The architect ________ designed this environmentally friendly building has won an international award.'
questions.answer: D) who

questions.question_text: Identify the type of sentence: 'Please turn off the lights before you leave the room.'
questions.answer: C) Imperative

questions.question_text: Choose the verb that agrees with the subject: 'Neither the principal nor the teachers ________ present at the seminar.'
questions.answer: B) were

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: 'My father is reading ________ fascinating book on the history of ancient India.'
questions.answer: A) a

questions.question_text: Identify the sentence that correctly transforms the direct speech 'I am reading a book,' said Nina, into indirect speech.
options: A) Nina said that she is reading a book.
B) Nina said that she was reading a book.
C) Nina says that she was reading a book.
D) Nina said if she was reading a book.
questions.answer: B) Nina said that she was reading a book.

questions.question_text: Select the correct active voice conversion for the passive sentence: 'The grand prize was won by our school choir.'
options: A) Our school choir has won the grand prize.
B) Our school choir had won the grand prize.
C) Our school choir won the grand prize.
D) Our school choir wins the grand prize.
questions.answer: C) Our school choir won the grand prize.

questions.question_text: Write a short paragraph on the topic 'The Importance of Reading Books in the Digital Age'. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: In today's digital era, reading books remains crucial as it enhances focus, vocabulary, and imagination. Unlike fleeting social media posts, books provide deep knowledge and critical thinking skills. Cultivating a reading habit reduces screen time and offers a peaceful escape, profoundly enriching our minds and perspectives.

questions.question_text: Write a diary entry expressing your feelings after winning the first prize in an inter-school debate competition. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Dear Diary, Today is the happiest day of my life! I won the first prize in the inter-school debate competition. When my name was announced, my heart swelled with pride. All my late-night preparations and rehearsals finally paid off. My parents and teachers were thrilled. I feel truly motivated to participate in more events. Goodnight!

questions.question_text: Read the extract from 'Somebody's Mother': 'She stood at the crossing and waited long, / Alone, uncared for, amid the throng.' What does the word 'throng' imply in these lines?
options: B) A large, densely packed crowd of people
C) A group of helpful children
D) A line of parked vehicles
questions.answer: B) A large, densely packed crowd of people

questions.question_text: In 'Verghese Kurien: I Too Had A Dream', what cooperative movement did Kurien champion to empower rural farmers?
questions.answer: B) The White Revolution (Operation Flood)

questions.question_text: According to the chapter 'A Concrete Example', what specific values did the protagonist demonstrate to inspire his local community? [25-35 words]
questions.answer: The protagonist demonstrated unwavering perseverance, selflessness, and sheer hard work. By building the road with his own hands, he showed the community that collective action and dedication can overcome the greatest obstacles.

questions.question_text: In 'The Wit that Won Hearts', how did Birbal cleverly solve the emperor's seemingly impossible riddle about counting the crows in the city? [25-35 words]
questions.answer: Birbal confidently gave a random number. He explained that if the count was higher, crows had visitors from other cities; if lower, some had gone on vacation, cleverly highlighting that wit matters more than exactness.

questions.question_text: Based on 'The Magic Brush of Dreams', what did the young artist do when the greedy emperor ordered him to paint gold? [25-35 words]
questions.answer: Instead of painting gold directly, the clever artist painted an ocean with a golden island. When the emperor demanded a ship to reach it, the artist painted a storm that ultimately swept the greedy emperor away.

questions.question_text: In 'Wisdom Paves the Way', what is the central message conveyed by the old traveler to the young merchant? [25-35 words]
questions.answer: The old traveler conveyed that true wealth is not just accumulated gold, but the wisdom, kindness, and experiences gathered over time. Wisdom helps navigate life's unexpected challenges far better than mere monetary riches.

questions.question_text: Discuss the legacy of Major Somnath Sharma as depicted in 'A Tale of Valour'. How does his sacrifice at the Battle of Badgam serve as an inspiration to the armed forces? [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Major Somnath Sharma's legacy is one of supreme sacrifice and fearless leadership. Despite a fractured arm and heavy enemy fire, he refused to abandon his post at Badgam. His final message, vowing to fight to the last man, epitomizes the highest traditions of the Indian Army, inspiring generations of soldiers with his immortal courage.

questions.question_text: Analyze the central theme of empathy and compassion in the poem 'Somebody's Mother'. How does the schoolboy's action reflect the poem's core message? [50-60 words]
questions.answer: The central theme is that compassion bridges the gap between strangers. While the crowd ignored the frail old woman, a cheerful schoolboy paused to help her cross the slippery street. His empathy stems from the realization that she is 'somebody's mother', hoping someone would similarly help his own mother in her time of need.
